question: The distance between the pole and the centre of curvature of a convex mirror is + 40 cm. What will be the distance between the pole and the focus of this mirror?
solution:
The correct answer is __**+ 20 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The distance between the **pole** (P) and the **center of curvature** (C) of a convex mirror is defined as the **radius of curvature** (R), which is given as **+ 40 cm**.
 
• The **focal length (f)** of a mirror is related to its radius of curvature (R) by the formula:

 **f = R / 2**
 
• Substituting the value of R = **+ 40 cm** into the formula:

 **f = 40 / 2 = + 20 cm**
 
• The **focal length** of a convex mirror is always positive because the focus lies on the same side as the reflective surface, as per the sign conventions in optics.
 
• **Hence, the distance between the pole and the focus of the convex mirror is + 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Mirror:**

 
 
• A convex mirror is a spherical mirror with the reflective surface bulging outward.
 
• It is also known as a **diverging mirror** because it spreads out light rays after reflection.
 
• Convex mirrors are commonly used in **rear-view mirrors** for vehicles and in surveillance systems.
 
 
 
• **Sign Conventions in Optics:**
 
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light (towards the reflective surface) are considered positive.
 
• Distances measured against the direction of the incident light are considered negative.
 
• For convex mirrors, the focal length (f) is always positive.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R) and Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• The radius of curvature is the distance from the pole to the center of curvature of the mirror.
 
• The focal length is half the radius of curvature: **f = R / 2**.
 
• This relationship applies to both convex and concave mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors provide a **wider field of view**, making them suitable for vehicle rear-view mirrors.
 
• They are used in **security mirrors** in stores to monitor large areas.
 
• In automated teller machines (ATMs), convex mirrors are installed for surveillance purposes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:**

 
 
• The mirror formula is:

 **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**

 where:
 
 
• **f** = focal length
 
• **v** = image distance
 
• **u** = object distance
 
 
 
• This formula is applicable for both convex and concave mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Positive Focal Length:**
 
 
• A positive focal length indicates that the focus lies on the same side as the reflective surface of the convex mirror.
 
• It also signifies that the mirror forms **virtual, upright, and diminished** images for all object positions.
